applicability: order, payment, delivery, and synchronization exceptions

applicability: service, logistics, finance, and workforce operations

applicability: data rights retention deletion and portability

applicability: AI prompt model and agent experiments

applicability: AI model prompt and agent evaluations
modality_independent_principles: Test whether the design can answer the stated decision question before exposing anyone: require a falsifiable hypothesis, appropriate control, unit and method of assignment, representative eligibility, stable measurement, exact treatment versions, primary outcome and guardrails, minimum meaningful effect, power or precision rationale, planned duration and analysis, interference and carryover assessment, and a decision policy that permits no-change or inconclusive outcomes.

applicability: data ownership, export and long-term access

Make authority contextual and consequence-sensitive: show that the same person may be owner, administrator, member, guest, child, delegate or viewer in different contexts; apply least privilege and deny by default; distinguish selection from invitation, authentication, consent, delegation and elevation; restate actor, tenant, resource and effect before consequential action; and require fresh verification or independent approval when policy and harm justify it.

Model provenance through versioned artifacts, activities and accountable contributors: record what was used, generated, transformed, selected, edited, approved and published; identify source and output versions, relevant roles, times and relationships; preserve interoperable lineage across export and recomposition; and distinguish evidence that a process or assertion is intact from judgments about truth, quality, legality, consent or ownership.

Separate contribution, authorship, ownership, accountability and disclosure: describe human creative contribution and organizational responsibility without crediting an automated tool as a moral or legal actor; avoid inferring rights from possession, prompting or metadata alone; record material assistance and source use; and make disclosure proportional to audience, context, deception risk, consequence and applicable obligation.

modality_independent_principles: Define a compositional contract before arranging components: establish content bounds, columns, gutters, outer margins, primary reading axes, alignment lines, module spans, vertical intervals, and the rules by which regions may nest, overlap, alternate, or break the grid.

Use span, position, scale, whitespace, and grouping to express semantic priority and dependency; modules that support comparison should share relevant alignment and dimensions, while modules with different roles should not be forced into visual equality.

Treat spacing as relational syntax: use repeatable intervals to bind labels to values, controls to affected content, items to groups, groups to sections, and sections to changes in task or argument; do not use generous whitespace without a structural or narrative purpose.

Begin with product truth and behavioral attributes: name the capability, audience, relationship, material, environment, or outcome the identity should make recognizable; translate each desired brand quality into observable choices and its opposite so adjectives such as premium, friendly, technical, calm, or bold cannot justify arbitrary styling.

Define one coherent brand grammar across typography, color, composition, shape, surface, imagery, iconography, motion, and voice; specify the recurring relationships, combinations, signature moments, and prohibited combinations that create recognition beyond a logo or isolated token.

Set expression levels by context and consequence: allow stronger identity in marketing, onboarding, discovery, empty states, and meaningful completion; reduce decorative intensity in frequent, dense, assistive, financial, security, health, error, permission, and irreversible work while preserving recognizable underlying grammar.

Define a form taxonomy before selecting radii or decoration: distinguish content, container, control, input, navigation, object, status, selection, overlay, evidence, and decorative shapes; assign each family a semantic purpose, interaction behavior, and relationship to the broader visual identity.

Specify a coherent geometric character through corner profile, curvature, angle, stroke, silhouette, proportion, cutout, and repetition while allowing semantic families to differ enough that controls, content, state, and decoration do not become interchangeable.

modality_independent_principles: Define a semantic surface model before styling components: name the base canvas, inset region, persistent panel, content container, interactive control, selected region, floating utility, transient overlay, blocking dialog, evidence frame, and atmospheric layer; specify which may occlude, receive focus, scroll, dismiss, persist, or contain another surface.

Use the smallest sufficient set of depth cues—tonal contrast, boundary, spacing, position, scale, shadow, blur, translucency, texture, and motion—and bind each cue to hierarchy, interaction, state, or atmosphere; do not let visual elevation imply semantic priority, certainty, security, or completion without supporting evidence.

Define the analytical contract before choosing a chart: name the question, decision, population, measure, unit, denominator, time window, comparison, aggregation, exclusions, freshness, source, uncertainty, and route to underlying records; do not let a visually compelling chart create a question or conclusion after the fact.

Choose visual form and encoding by task and data relationship: use position and aligned length for precise comparison, preserve time order and interval, distinguish part-to-whole from change and distribution, limit simultaneous encodings, and prefer a labeled value, table, or small multiple when a chart adds interpretation cost without analytical benefit.

Keep scope and comparison visible with the result: show active filters, segmentation, period, baseline, target or threshold, series identity, units, missing data, and material definition changes; bind summary values to the visualization and detail that explain them.

Define a state model before styling: identify the object, actor, lifecycle, interaction, availability, validation, severity, freshness, synchronization, permission, and completion dimensions; name mutually exclusive states and valid transitions so one color, badge, or adjective is not forced to represent several different facts.

Give every material state a canonical name, plain-language meaning, entry condition, permitted actions, next states, persistence, timestamp or freshness where relevant, and recovery path; use the same semantics across component, list, detail, notification, activity, and audit views.

Encode state redundantly through an appropriate combination of text, icon, shape, contrast, position, boundary, surface, motion, and programmatic semantics; preserve visible focus and never rely on color, opacity, hover, animation, or disabled appearance alone.

Define the purpose of every motion event before choosing timing or effect: classify it as feedback, state change, spatial continuity, hierarchy, attention guidance, progress, direct manipulation, teaching, or bounded expression; identify the affected object, initiating action, information conveyed, next task, frequency, consequence, cancellation, and non-motion equivalent.

Reserve expressive motion for low-frequency and meaningful moments whose emotional or brand role is explicit; keep routine, dense, assistive, financial, health, security, permission, error, and irreversible workflows efficient and restrained, and never let celebration overstate completion, safety, value, or user consent.

modality_independent_principles: Define a canonical vocabulary before polishing tone: name each important object, action, role, state, scope, and consequence once; use the same term wherever the same concept appears, distinguish terms when concepts differ, and document prohibited aliases, ambiguous verbs, and domain terms that require explanation.

Keep voice stable and adapt tone to context: express a consistent product character while changing warmth, urgency, brevity, and formality according to the person's likely state, task frequency, consequence, uncertainty, and need for reassurance; reduce personality as risk, distress, or irreversibility increases.

Structure language around the person's task: lead with the information or decision needed now, use familiar and concrete words, keep sentences and paragraphs scannable, reveal detail progressively, and place explanation where it supports rather than interrupts action.

Calibrate claims and recommendations to evidence: distinguish observed facts, estimates, predictions, suggestions, and decisions; identify uncertainty, important assumptions, source or freshness when material, and who remains responsible; never use confident language, celebration, or authority cues to overstate safety, completion, consent, or likely outcomes.

Write for accessibility and translation from the start: provide visible labels and instructions, avoid meaning carried only by position, color, idiom, humor, or cultural shorthand, keep grammatical structures direct, leave room for expansion, and test assistive announcements and localized variants in their actual interface context.

Govern verbal design as a product system: maintain the vocabulary, voice attributes, tone matrix, message patterns, examples, ownership, review triggers, localization notes, and measurement plan; review language with design, research, accessibility, legal, support, and domain experts according to consequence rather than treating copy as final-stage polish.

Treat figures and tables as evidence-bearing document components: state the question or takeaway, identify what is measured and its scope, use captions and headers, keep data structures simple enough to navigate, provide equivalent text or accessible data, cite the specific source and freshness, and separate interpretation from the underlying values.

Make document authority and revision state visible: identify owner, status, version or date, applicable scope, source references, approval state, superseded editions, change history, and canonical location; keep these signals in machine-readable metadata and perceivable content where consequential, and verify that exports do not detach them from the work.

Validate the delivered artifact, not only the source or visual proof: combine automated checks with manual inspection of structure, sequence, headings, tables, figures, links, metadata, language, reflow, keyboard and assistive navigation, print output, and representative reader tasks after every conversion or assembly step.

Translate brand and message into an art-direction grammar rather than a mood label: specify subject behavior, environment, viewpoint, distance, focal hierarchy, geometry, negative space, light, color, contrast, depth, texture, finish, realism, imperfection, and prohibited treatments with reference examples and reasons.

Choose subjects and moments for contextual truth: prefer real, specific, plausible activity and environments over generic symbolism; represent people with agency, dignity, diversity, and relevant context; obtain informed permission when required, avoid tokenism and stereotypes, and disclose staged, composite, generated, or materially altered imagery when that distinction matters.

Design from a platform-context matrix rather than device names: enumerate available window size, aspect, orientation, posture, viewing distance, density, text scale, locale, input set, precision, hover, hardware keyboard, system chrome, safe areas, multitasking, performance, connectivity, and assistive settings; derive layout and interaction changes from capabilities and constraints.

Test complete tasks across a representative platform matrix: include minimum and maximum windows, intermediate resize, orientation and posture changes, split screen, large text, localization, high contrast, reduced motion, screen reader, keyboard-only, pointer, touch, stylus where supported, interruption, offline, denied capability, restore, multi-window, performance, and upgrade; verify functional parity and intentional differences.
